cards.title: Introduction to Vue Components
cards.content:
Components are one of the most powerful features of Vue.js. They help you extend basic HTML elements to encapsulate reusable code.

At a high level, components are custom elements that Vue's compiler attaches behavior to. In Vue, a component is essentially a reusable Vue instance with a name.

cards.title: Anatomy of a Single File Component
cards.content:
Vue SFCs (Single File Components) group the HTML, JavaScript, and CSS in a single file using the .vue extension.

<template>
  <div class="greeting">{{ msg }}</div>
</template>

<script>
export default {
  data() {
    return { msg: 'Hello Vue!' }
  }
}
</script>

<style scoped>
.greeting { color: red; }
</style>

cards.title: Passing Data with Props
cards.content:
Props are custom attributes you can register on a component. When a value is passed to a prop attribute, it becomes a property on that component instance.

To pass data from a parent to a child component, we use props down.

cards.title: Listening to Child Events
cards.content:
While parents can pass data down via props, children must communicate back up to parents using events.

Inside the child component, you can emit an event using this.$emit('custom-event') and listen to it on the parent using @custom-event.

cards.title: Content Distribution with Slots
cards.content:
Vue implements a content distribution API inspired by the Web Components spec draft, using the <slot> element to serve as distribution outlets for content.

This allows you to pass template fragments down to the child component to render dynamically.

cards.title: Summary of Vue Components
cards.content:
Vue components give us modular, maintainable, and reusable blocks of UI.

Remember: Props down, events up! Use slots for flexible content composition, and SFCs to keep your markup, logic, and styles cleanly separated yet co-located.
